item.title: C/C++ Static Variable Storage: DATA vs BSS Segment Placement and Linkage
item.description:
“C/C++ Static Variable Storage: DATA vs BSS Segment Placement and Linkage”

Location of Static Variables: DATA vs BSS

The storage allocation for a static variable hinges on whether it receives an explicit, non-zero initial value. Program memory is generally partitioned into segments; the .DATA and .BSS segments are specifically designated for global and static data.

The primary distinction is:

  1. .DATA Segment: This area stores static and global variables that are explicitly initialized to non-zero values at compile time. Data here is loaded with initial values when the program starts.
  2. .BSS (Block Started by Symbol) Segment: This area holds variables that are uninitialized or explicitly initialized to zero (0 or 0x0). The operating system or loader typically initializes this entire memory block to zeros before program execution begins, saving space in the executable file.
